bad.why: It is used only of nosy questioning, never of actual digging or weeding.

mean: to gamble on what will come up in an exam
lit: to stake on 'the mountain': to bet everything on one guessed spot

use.how: Usually about tests: 山をかけて勉強する, 山をかけたところが出た/外れた. Often written ヤマをかける; also used of guessing interview questions.

cue: With one night left before the history exam, you study only the Meiji period and hope that is what the test asks about.

ctx.s: テストで{山[やま]をかけたら}、見事[みごと]に当[あ]たった。
ctx.en: I gambled on what would be on the test, and I guessed right.

ctx.s: 「どこに{山[やま]をかける}？」「やっぱり第三章[だいさんしょう]かな」
ctx.en: "What are you betting will come up?" "Chapter three, I reckon."

ctx.s: {山[やま]をかけた}ところが全然[ぜんぜん]出[で]なくて、散々[さんざん]だった。
ctx.en: None of the parts I'd bet on came up, and it was a disaster.

ctx.s: 時間[じかん]がないので、出[で]そうな問題[もんだい]に{山[やま]をかけて}勉強[べんきょう]した。
ctx.en: Short of time, I just studied the questions I guessed were likely to come up.

ctx.s: 弟[おとうと]はいつも{山[やま]をかけて}ばかりで、まじめに全部[ぜんぶ]復習[ふくしゅう]しない。
ctx.en: My brother always just gambles on a few topics and never revises everything properly.

ctx.s: 面接[めんせつ]で聞[き]かれそうな質問[しつもん]に{山[やま]をかけて}、答[こた]えを準備[じゅんび]した。
ctx.en: I guessed which questions the interviewers were likely to ask and prepared answers for those.

bad.s: 夏休[なつやす]みに家族[かぞく]で{山[やま]をかけて}、富士山[ふじさん]に登[のぼ]った。
bad.en: (meant: we went on a mountain trip in the summer and climbed Mount Fuji)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with real mountains. It means betting on which topics will come up.

bad.s: 試験[しけん]の範囲[はんい]を全部[ぜんぶ]しっかり{山[やま]をかけて}勉強[べんきょう]した。
bad.en: (meant: I studied the whole syllabus thoroughly)
bad.why: It means gambling on a few likely topics instead of covering everything, the opposite of thorough study.
